question: Land revenue systems under British rule varied regionally. Which land revenue system was primarily followed in Bombay and Madras Presidencies?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ryotwari system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ryotwari system** was primarily followed in the **Bombay** and **Madras Presidencies**.
 
• In this system, the revenue settlement was made directly with the **cultivators or ryots**. They were recognized as the owners of the land.
 
• The cultivators were required to pay land revenue directly to the government annually. *Hence, statement regarding Ryotwari system is correct.*
 
• The **British administration**, under the Ryotwari system, collected revenue based on the fertility of the soil, type of crop grown, and irrigation facilities available.
 
• The system was introduced by **Thomas Munro**, a British official, during the early 19th century in regions like Madras.
 
• **Ryots** had the freedom to cultivate their land, but the system often led to exploitation due to high revenue demands by the British. *Hence, it had both advantages and disadvantages.*
 
• ***Thus, the Ryotwari system was the primary land revenue system in Bombay and Madras Presidencies.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Details of Land Revenue Systems:**

 
 
• **Ryotwari system:**

 
 
• Introduced in **Madras**, **Bombay**, and **Assam**.
 
• The ownership of land was vested directly in the **ryots** or cultivators.
 
• The government collected revenue directly from the ryots based on the nature of the land.
 
• While it recognized individual ownership, excessive revenue demand often led to the exploitation of farmers.
 
 
 
• **Zamindari system:**
 
 
• Implemented in **Bengal Presidency**.
 
• Land revenue was collected through intermediaries called **zamindars**, who acted as landlords.
 
• Zamindars were responsible for collecting revenue from peasants and paying it to the British.
 
• This system led to the creation of a wealthy class of zamindars, but peasants faced exploitation.
 
 
 
• **Mahalwari system:**
 
 
• Introduced in **North-Western Provinces**, **Punjab**, and parts of **Central India**.
 
• Revenue settlements were made with entire villages or communities, referred to as **mahals**.
 
• Land revenue was shared among the village community based on collective ownership.
 
• It aimed at balancing individual and community ownership but often faced administrative challenges.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Key features of Ryotwari system:**
 
 
• Introduced by **Thomas Munro** in **1820**.
 
• It recognized the **individual ownership** of ryots over land.
 
• Revenue was determined based on land fertility and other factors.
 
• Ryots had the freedom to cultivate their land but were often burdened by high taxes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison of Land Revenue Systems:**

 
 
• **Ryotwari system:** Direct settlement with cultivators; prevalent in Madras and Bombay Presidencies.
 
• **Zamindari system:** Settlement with zamindars; prevalent in Bengal Presidency.
 
• **Mahalwari system:** Settlement with village communities; prevalent in North-Western Provinces and Punjab.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Farmers:**
 
 
• Excessive revenue demands under Ryotwari and Zamindari systems led to exploitation and indebtedness.
 
• Mahalwari system was intended to promote community ownership but faced administrative challenges.
